What does an unfilled appointment cost your business?

Start with booked appointments for a representative month and calculate what share customers missed. Remove the share of those spaces you managed to refill. Multiply the unfilled spaces by average appointment value for an estimate of exposed revenue, and by average duration for unfilled hours. A lower target no-show rate gives you a second scenario under the same refill assumptions.

Monthly revenue at risk = appointments × no-show rate × share left unfilled × appointment value

Manage salon appointments and reminders on Shopify →

Worked example

A studio schedules 120 monthly appointments at $75 each and records a 10% no-show rate. Twelve visits are missed. If three of those spaces are refilled, nine go unfilled, leaving $675 in appointment revenue at risk. With 45-minute visits, that is 6 hours and 45 minutes of unused appointment time.

No-Show Cost Calculator FAQ

How do I calculate the no-show rate from my booking records?

Divide missed appointments by scheduled appointments for the same period, then multiply by 100. Eight missed visits out of 160 booked gives a 5% rate. Use the same definition in later comparisons.

Should I count a cancellation that another customer took?

Keep a consistent definition of what counts as missed. If you include a released appointment and another customer fills the space, reflect it in the refill share so the model does not treat it as empty.

Why can the expected number of empty appointments include a fraction?

Rates are applied to a typical month. A result of 4.5 unfilled appointments represents an average across months, even though each individual appointment is a whole booking.

Is revenue at risk the same as lost profit?

Revenue at risk values the unfilled appointment at its average selling price. A retained deposit, an avoided material cost or paid work completed in the time changes the financial effect on your business.

Can I compare reminders with a waitlist strategy?

Use a lower target missed-appointment rate to explore a reminder scenario. Change the refill percentage in a separate run to see what filling more openings could recover. Keep a note of the assumptions for each run.

How should a seasonal business read the annual figure?

The annual figure extends the modelled month across 12 months. A ski school or summer tour operator can estimate peak and quiet months separately, then combine the periods that match its actual season.
